extracted.intended_audience: JD students and law students preparing for patent practice (U.S. patent drafting and prosecution)
extracted.subtask_description: A law school course teaching students how to prepare, draft, and prosecute U.S. patent applications (utility and design), respond to office actions, conduct examiner interviews, and plan foreign counterpart prosecution, with practical drafting and mock-exercise components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare effective U.S. utility patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn how to prepare effective U.S. utility patent applications (classes 1-6). As part of this, each student will draft patent claims and then a complete patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on drafting both claims and a complete application; practical exercises occur in classes 1–6. (No further examples/anti-patterns provided on page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecute U.S. utility patent applications through grant
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn how to prosecute U.S. utility patent applications through grant and key considerations along the way (classes 7-12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the prosecution lifecycle and strategic considerations encountered between filing and allowance; practical prosecution topics are taught in classes 7–12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond effectively to rejections (office actions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn to respond effectively to rejections of U.S. utility patent applications (classes 8-12). As part of this, each student will draft a complete response to a real patent office action rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hands-on drafting of a complete response to an actual office action is required; teaches substantive and tactical reply techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview patent examiners concerning rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn to interview patent examiners concerning rejections of U.S. utility patent applications (class 11). As part of this, each student will draft a request for a patent examiner interview, participate in a (mock) patent examiner interview, and draft a summary of that interview.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes drafting an interview request, conducting a mock interview, and preparing an interview summary—practical training in examiner communication and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine approaches to amending/strengthening granted patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn to determine the best approach for amending and/or strengthening granted patents (class 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers post-grant amendment strategies and methods to strengthen enforceability or scope of granted patents; class 13 focuses on these topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize opportunities and consequences of challenging third-party patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn to recognize opportunities for and consequences of challenging third-party patents in patent office (class 13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaches when and how to pursue inter partes or other PTO-based challenges and the tradeoffs/risks associated with such proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize opportunities for design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn to recognize opportunities for design patents (class 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers when design patent protection is appropriate and how it differs from utility patent practice; addressed in class 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and schedule foreign counterpart patent prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Students will learn to plan and schedule foreign counterpart patent prosecution (class 14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes timeline and strategic considerations for filing and prosecuting foreign counterpart applications and coordinating international prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Course assessment and logistical structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Course details: Units 3; Grading Options: Numeric or CR/D/F; Exam Type: In-class Exam; Writing Requirement: No; Skills/Experiential Requirement: Yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the course is skills/experiential with practical exercises (drafting, responses, mock interviews). Assessment may be numeric or credit/no-credit/fail; culminates in an in-class exam in addition to experiential assignments.
